newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE BLANK RED WINGS 6-0 TO NARROW SERIES TO 3-2.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-AVALANCHE BLANK RED WINGS 6-0 TO NARROW SERIES TO 3-2.

text.p: Claude Lemieux and Joe Sakic each scored twice and Patrick Roy recorded his third shutout of the playoffs as the Colorado Avalanche blanked the Detroit Red Wings 6-0 Saturday to cut their deficit in the Western Conference finals to 3-2.
Lemieux got the first two goals of the game to send the Avalanche on their way. Stephane Yelle and Scott Young also scored as the defending champions avoided elimination.
Game 6 of the best-of-seven series is Monday at Detroit.
Blanked in Game 4 by a 6-0 score, the Avalanche drove Mike Vernon from the Detroit net less than three minutes into the second period with the score 4-0.

Lemieux, held to one goal in the first four games of the series, got it started at 6:46 of the first period. Vernon was never able to get to his feet after stopping a Valeri Kamensky backhander and Lemieux wristed the puck home from just above the crease.

Detroit's best scoring chance came midway through the opening period when Darren McCarty missed the net on a clear breakaway. Seconds later, Roy denied McCarty on a point-blank chance to keep Colorado ahead.

Lemieux scored again with 8:56 to go in the period. Vernon stopped a point shot by Sandis Ozolinsh but Lemieux chipped in the rebound for his 13th playoff goal, tying the career high he set two years ago en route to the Conn Smythe Trophy.
Sakic broke in with Lemieux on a 2-on-1 and held the puck before wristing it between Vernon's pads from the low left faceoff circle to make it 3-0 with 4:26 to play.

Yelle, who missed the first three games of the series with a knee injury, got his first playoff goal 2:23 into the second to end Vernon's night. His hard wrist shot from the right circle tipped off Vernon's blocker into the net.
Vernon, who faced only 10 shots, was pulled for just the second time in the playoffs.

Chris Osgood, relegated to backup status in the postseason, looked sharp early, but surrendered Sakic's second goal midway through the second period. Sakic cut off the right boards and across the slot before whipping a wrister just under the crossbar for his eighth of the playoffs.

Young's goal with 1:56 to go in the period closed the scoring. He was left unchecked in front of Osgood and shoveled his own rebound over the goalie's right pad for his third playoff goal and second of the series.
Roy was rarely tested the rest of the way in wrapping up his 11th career playoff shutout. He has allowed one goal or less in seven of nine postseason home games.
